A lot of people, both on and off X, keep asking me the same question:

What's your honest outlook on crypto?

And the truth is, I think most people aren't ready for my answer.

1. Don't expect anything remotely similar to what we've experienced over the past few years. That era is over.

2. We're entering an entirely new paradigm driven by AI. Capital, attention, and investment priorities are shifting.

3. Crypto cycles won't behave the way they used to. Those blindly relying on historical patterns and the traditional four-year cycle are going to get burned.

4. Most of the major milestones crypto was supposed to achieve have already happened. ETFs, institutional adoption, mainstream recognition. It's becoming increasingly difficult to generate the same level of excitement through new narratives.

5. Crypto isn't dead. But I genuinely believe the way we've experienced crypto cycles is.

And here's what I think very few people understand:

The next decade won't necessarily reward the people who made money in the last one.

The market is evolving, and the strategies that worked before may become completely irrelevant.

I expect a much more selective market, with capital increasingly concentrated in a smaller number of projects that actually deliver value.

The days when almost everything pumped simply because Bitcoin was going up may be coming to an end.

Crypto isn't disappearing.

It's maturing.

And I believe that transition will be incredibly painful for those who refuse to adapt.

Hope you understand.

Data breach involving Skladon

On 15 November, Skladon, one of our delivery partners, notified us that an attacker had gained unauthorized access to Trezor order data it holds. We’re still investigating with Skladon, but we want to let you know now.

What we know:
• We believe the data for about 27,000 orders placed between 9 August and 7 November was exported.
• It includes name, phone number, address, email and order details.
• Skladon delivers to many countries, so this isn’t limited to one region.
• Trezor systems were not compromised, and your device is secure. 

Who is affected:
• If you received our email today and ordered between 9 August and 7 November, your details were part of this incident.
• A small number of customers who ordered between 9 and 14 August may also be affected, but we can’t email them: their details had already been anonymized in our systems.
• Skladon does not ship to the US, so customers there are not affected. 

Treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about your order as suspicious, and be alert to potential risks to your physical security. Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup.

From today, anonymous pickup is live in 18 European countries, so you can order without giving us your home address. We’re also shortening our data retention period from 90 days to 45 (and plan to reduce it further), and we’re requiring our shipping partners to follow the same policy.

We’re deeply sorry this has happened.

Full details and FAQs: https://trezor.io/blog/news/data-breach-at-trezor-shipping-partner-skladon

I believe the next few decades will bring a massive shift in how we value assets.

While everyone is obsessed with AI, technology, and digital assets, I think some of the biggest opportunities will be found in the physical world.

Land. Farmland. Precious metals. Energy. Water. Natural resources.

Things that are finite, essential, and impossible to replicate with a few lines of code.

Technology can scale almost infinitely. Physical resources cannot.

And as AI and automation continue to expand, the demand for energy, infrastructure, and raw materials could become even more important.

The next great wealth transfer might not be about owning the next big technology.

It might be about owning the scarce resources that technology depends on.
